content:
maya: Quick follow-up from todays call: we need a concrete plan for billing_key propagation vs metric cardinality. Two conflicting goals: exact per-tenant chargeback vs keeping Prom/metrics sane.
harry: +1. naive approach (attach billing_key label to every metric) will blow up TSDB. not acceptable.
cleo: we already saw spikes when we added session_id to a subset of gauges. cardinality kills ingestion and query perf.
maya: proposals on table: 1) traces-only billing propagation (keep metrics aggregated), 2) hashed-bucket metrics (N=256) keyed by billing_bucket, 3) sampled trace-backed accounting with scaling factors.
devin: option 2 seems promising: metrics use billing_bucket label (low-card) and traces carry the actual billing_key for exact reconciliation. then nightly rollups reconcile sampled traces to full traffic using scale factors.
harry: agree but edge: bursts and short-lived keys. reconciliation needs to handle skew quickly so we don't misbill. also need to surface uncertainty margin.
cleo: operational concerns: how to pick N for buckets? and collision model: two big tenants colliding in same bucket could hide burst costs. maybe we should reserve explicit per-tenant counters for top-K tenants (by spend).
maya: reserve top-K + hashed buckets for rest = hybrid. will need a cheap LRU to promote/demote tenants from bucket->explicit counter.
ops-bot: ops-bot: queued query: `series_count by billing_bucket over 7d` will post results in ~10m :mag_right: 
devin: sampling design: keep deterministic sampling keyed by billing_key so scale factors are stable. store sample_rate per-key in metadata store.
harry: also want a quick reconcile endpoint for invoices so finance can request higher-fidelity runs on demand for a date range. run a targeted trace rehydrate using raw spans.
cleo: span schema changes: add `billing.key` (string), `billing.bucket` (int), `billing.sample_rate` (float), and `billing.reconciled=true|false`. include in OTLP examples.
maya: example span attrs: ```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "billing.key": "acct_42",
    "billing.bucket": "17",
    "billing.sample_rate": "0.01"
  }
}
```
devin: what about metrics emitted by infra (cache hits, gpu-hours)? they should follow same hybrid: explicit labels for reserved accounts + bucket for others; and emit a tag `billing_resolved=true|false` when reconciliation is pending.
harry: alerting: add alert if top-K promotion churn > X per hour (means buckets unstable) and if reconciliation backlog > Y hours.
cleo: data retention: keep full trace-level billing info for 90 days; aggregated metrics for 13 months. that balances auditability and cost.
maya: privacy/legal: billing.key is sensitive-ish. encrypt in transit (OTLP gRPC) and at rest; restrict full-billing-span access to finance+billing SRE role.
devin: flow for late-arriving billing keys (e.g., auth service delayed): record span with billing.key missing -> emit `billing.missing=true` metric and a trace-level log with trace_id; downstream pipeline will attempt enrichment with user lookup store within 5 minutes. if enrichment fails, mark as unallocated and roll into default bucket.
harry: integrations: Datadog/Prom exports should map billing_bucket -> tag and avoid exporting raw billing_key. For invoice generation, run trace-backed reconciliation job that pulls full spans from trace store.
cleo: action items: 1) maya to write RFC addendum describing hybrid buckets + top-K reserve (due Tue), 2) devin to draft span schema PR + OTLP examples (due Mon), 3) ops to run cardinality sim with N={64,256,1024} to estimate series count and storage (ops-bot to post results), 4) harry to spec reconciliation job and API for finance.
maya: +1 on action items. leaning to N=256 and top-K=200 as a starting point.
ops-bot: ops-bot: posted cardinality sim summary -> https://ops-reports/internal/cardinality-sim-4012351234 :bar_chart: 
devin: I'll include deterministic sampling pseudo-code in the PR: `sample = hash(billing.key) % (1/sample_rate) == 0` so sampling is stable across services.
harry: one more: track a vanity counter `billing.estimated_error_pct` in invoice pipeline so finance knows confidence bounds.
maya: ok scheduling 30m follow-up Wednesday to finalize RFC addendum. thanks all.
